title: embodiment
content_html:
embodiment

What can a body know by placing a hand on something or changing its position? The reach of a hand matters in making an ink drawing in hand life. The distance from a work in body space matters in seeing it. Both kinds of encounter raise a question that becomes stranger in Nerve. How do we come to attribute bodily feeling to a figure that has a shape and no sensation? Body space 1 · Embodied mind

Reading note. Existentialism. Beauvoir begins The Ethics of Ambiguity with the difficulty of being a subject to oneself and an object in the lives of others. A work from body space raises an analogous question about position. What changes when we become aware of where we are looking from as well as where the body we see appears to be? The Ethics of Ambiguity, part I
